pa.s: 3. SOURCE ROCK EVALUATION. Source rock horizons have been identified using RockEval pyrolysis and total organic carbon (TOC) measurements. The samples investigated are from the Cretaceous Asgard Fm. and from the Lower Carboniferous. DC samples were hand- picked for coal, coaly shale or dark material and this fraction was

organic matter which is preserved in sedimentary rocks. Under the increasing influence of temperature and time (maturation), most kerogen produce hydrocarbons. TOC Total Organic Carbon: measure of the organic carbon in rock. expressed as weight per cent. Used as fundamental parameter in source rock classification. RockEval A commercial technique for the anhy

r Carboniferous section (4268- 4295m) show no source rock potential. One SWC sample at 4330m is very rich in organic matter, it has an S2 value of 87 kg/tonne, TOC of 42% and Hydrogen index of 208 mgHC/gTOC. These data indicates that this sample contains Type III kerogen, and that it has potential for gaseous hydrocarbon generation. The samples in the interv

ere to obtain maturity profile of the well using vitrinite reflectance and spore color, and to identify and characterize potential source rocks in the RockEval/TOC.
